title: Start with a cube
description: Make one solid: a cube, 20 mm on each side. The three numbers are X, Y and Z. Everything we add later will build on this starting point.
code:
// Units: mm. PCB stand worked example.
cube([20, 20, 20]);

title: Resize it into a flat base
description: Change the three dimensions. cube() can make a rectangular block too. Our base is now 81.406 × 86.740 mm and only 3 mm thick: the PCB outline plus 4 mm on each edge.
code:
// Units: mm. PCB stand worked example.
cube([81.406, 86.740, 3]);

title: Move the base around the board origin
description: Add translate([-4, -4, 0]). The whole base moves 4 mm in negative X and Y; its size stays the same. The origin will be the bottom-left corner of our PCB. Compare the base with the red and green axes.

title: Subtract a block to open the middle
description: Wrap the base in difference(), then add a second block as the cutter. The first shape stays; the second is removed. The cutter starts below the base and ends above it, so the window goes all the way through.

title: Add the first mounting post
description: Use union() to join a cylinder to the frame. translate() places it at the first PCB hole. The post tapers from a wide 12 mm foot to an 8 mm top. d1 sets the bottom diameter; d2 sets the top. Starting at Z=2.8 overlaps the 3 mm base by 0.2 mm; the top is at Z=9.

title: Add a second post
description: Keep the first post. Add another cylinder at X=4.318, Y=75.438. Only its Y position changes. These coordinates come from the real board, so we do not guess the distance from the corners.

title: Add the two posts on the other side
description: Add two more cylinders at X=69.596, using the same two Y coordinates. Now all four mounting positions have supports. The posts are still solid.

title: Cut a screw hole through the first post
description: Put the whole frame-and-posts shape inside a new difference(). A 3.4 mm cylinder removes material through the first post AND the base, from Z=-0.1 to Z=9.1. Try Top view to see the hole.

title: Cut the other three screw holes
description: Keep the first cutter and add three more at the remaining mounting positions. The stand now has four through-holes. This is the finished shape; check the actual screw fit with the small test piece before printing it.

title: Make the repeated code shorter
description: The shape stays exactly the same. Store the four positions in holes, then use for (p = holes) to repeat the post and cutter. p[0] is X and p[1] is Y. Go Back to compare this with the four separate copies.
